canon.role_in_story: A lanternfolk lineage lost its fungal colony and grew a mineral bloom in the wound instead. That cost the species most of its life and handed back the one path its symbiosis had closed, and it made her subspecies the control case: the only body in the setting where what a colony does and what a colony prevents can both be measured on the same person. That is a scientific arrangement and everyone involved agreed to it. The arrangement has one consequence nobody costed, and it is not about her body at all. The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and the frame is what it reads through. Between a lanternfolk and a deadlight the frame gives one signal: a living hyphal colony. She has none. She grew around a silicate lattice instead, which is inert and does not answer. So the one method in the setting that can tell her kind from her parent's cannot tell her at all, and the register enters her as a lanternfolk. That is not a clerical error that a sympathetic clerk could amend. It is the method working exactly as designed on a body the method was never built to hold, and there is no second method, because the second method is the village remembering and the register's entire reason for existing is that the village may amend its own dead. So the only body in this setting that can be told apart from its parent by anyone standing next to her is filed by the one instrument that is supposed to know, and she has no standing to correct the file, because the correction would have to be an entry and the entry is the thing that is wrong. That is her whole condition and it is institutional before it is anything else: she is not unaffiliated because her body cannot do something. It is because the setting has one instrument for the question she is, the instrument has answered, and the answer is filed. Her species has no ceiling at all and closes nothing, and she is on no ladder, and neither of those facts has anything to do with it.
canon.first_appearance: Read out of the cavern-side register at a settlement hearing, in the flat voice the college uses for entries it does not embellish. The household had come to ask after a grandmother who was entered as the grandmother's own sister, because both women were entered the same way, and the clerk who read the line did not look up, and Nessa was the one who had come down with them and who was not in the book at all under the name anyone in the room knew her by. She waited until the reading was finished before she said anything, and what she said was not a correction. She asked whether the register had ever held a line for a body with a bloom instead of a colony, and the clerk said the column was not a column, it was a reading, and there was nothing to write in that box.
canon.lore:
A deadlight is a lanternfolk that lost its fungal colony and grew a mineral bloom in the wound, and the subspecies record is unusually plain about the trade: two hundred and fifty years of life given up, and the mind path handed back, because the thing that was closing it is the thing that is gone. Nothing now answers introspection from inside her. The bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is a structurally different arrangement from a colony and, the record says plainly, structurally unconstrained by it. So there is no ceiling. Not a high one, not a distant one. Her species has no ceiling at all and it closes no path, which is a statement about a limit and not a statement about a ladder, and it is worth being exact about that here because it is the fact most often read backwards. She is not unaffiliated because nothing is available to her. Something is available to her. What has happened is that the setting has one instrument for the question of what she is, the instrument has already answered, and nobody has come back to look.

The instrument is the Field Registry. Its method is stated without any apology: at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and the reason is that the record of a life is also the record of a gate that was never available to it. The mortuary college does not soften this and does not vary it. It reads the frame. Between the parent species and the subspecies there is exactly one signal the frame can give, and it is the living colony, because a colony is what a lanternfolk body is. A deadlight does not have one. She has a silicate lattice where the hyphal threads were, and it is inert, and it does not answer, and that inertness is the whole of the difference and is also the whole of the problem. So a body carrying the bloom is entered as a body carrying the colony. The entry is not wrong by accident. It is the method encountering the one case it does not hold, and answering, in the only voice it has.

She went down to the hearing as a witness and came back as the subject of it, which is how she learned that the register's problem is not confined to funerals. The reading had entered her grandmother as her grandmother's sister. Two women, entered identically, because both were read through a frame that reports the same absence in the same way. Nobody had falsified anything. Somebody had been accurate, consistently, using the correct method, about a body that the method does not distinguish.

The obvious remedy is the village. It is ruled out by the register's founding reason. A village that may amend its dead may amend its standing, and a record that its own community can edit is not a record of anything. That is not a preference. It is the argument the college was founded on, and it has held for longer than she has been alive. So the second method is the one thing this setting has explicitly refused itself, and she is the case the refusal was correct for and wrong about at the same time.

Here is what makes it a life rather than an administrative curiosity. She is the best thing in the caverns at being looked at in the dark, because she can see, and her parent cannot, and that is the single most-cited difference between the two and the reason the subspecies carries the name it does. It is a real advantage and it is available to her anywhere, and it has been available to her for her whole life with no institution anywhere in the setting interested in it. Being the only person who can see is worth nothing to a college that reads bodies for what is inside them. The discipline that would make her valuable is precisely the discipline that produced the instrument that cannot tell her from her mother's cousin.

She has read the whole of the college's method. She can do it better than the clerk who entered her grandmother, because she knows what the frame reports and what it does not, and she has said so in writing, and the writing is filed. The college charges for the file. This is its standing revenue and not its failure, which she understands and has no argument against. She has stopped bringing it up. What she does instead is go down to the hearings, which is where the reading happens aloud, and she stands at the back, and she waits for her own kind to be entered as somebody else. She has never once corrected one in front of the household, because a household that is told its grandmother was misfiled will want the entry changed, and an entry changed is a village amending its dead, and the whole apparatus she is trying to correct is built on the fact that nobody ever will.

She is not bitter and should not be drawn as a tragic figure. The arrangement is correct about her grandmother and wrong about her, and she can state both halves without collapsing either. She is not seeking a rung. She is not on a ladder and her species has no ceiling to be climbing toward. She is trying to get one line of a book rewritten, and the reason she cannot is that the book exists in order not to be rewritten, and she understands the reason, and the understanding does not help.
history: Born in the caverns to a parent kind whose colony failed in her infancy and was replaced by a mineral bloom in the wound, which is a survival and is not described as one.

Understood early that she was entered in the register beside her grandmother and entered identically, and worked out later that this was the frame reporting accurately rather than a clerk making a mistake.
Found the difference between her kind and her parent's by the only means available to her, which is that she can see in the dark and they cannot.
Wrote to the mortuary college setting out the whole of the method and what it cannot distinguish, and the writing was filed, and the college charges for the file.
Stopped arguing at the hearings and began standing at the back of them, on the ground that an amendment made in a room full of a household is a village amending its dead.

relationships.note: Lanternfolk whose colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, which cost the species most of its life and gave back the one path the symbiosis had closed. She is the only body in the setting where what a colony does and what a colony prevents can both be measured on the same person, and she was entered in the register as somebody else while that measurement was being taken.

Her parent kind, and the reason the register's failure is total rather than partial: the frame gives one signal between them and she does not carry it. Neither of them can leave the caves, so the difference between them has never once been established by one of them walking away.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, because a village that may amend its dead may amend its standing. Its method is correct, its reason is sound, and it has no column for a body that grew around something inert instead of something alive, so she is filed as her parent's cousin.

The prize in that dispute is whether a body may be entered in the register at all, and it cannot be split because the frame distinguishes the two kinds by a colony that dies. She is the body on which that reasoning runs true and comes out wrong, which is the shape of a dispute that has no side she can be on.

Neither her kind nor her parent's can leave the cave systems for exactly the reason the parent cannot, and only one of them can see. The ground holds both populations, neither has anywhere else to be, and the arrangement has therefore never once been tested by somebody declining to participate.

A mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because certifying a death needs a body and the frames keep producing the record without it. She is alive and already entered wrongly, which is a cheaper version of the same problem and has not been thought about as one.

reference_stats.summary: She is not a fighter and would not be described as one by anyone who has watched her decline an invitation. She is the best reader of a frame in the ground she can reach, because she has had to learn what a frame reports by being misread by one, and she is the only person in the caverns who can find anything at all in the dark. What she can do is look accurately at the inside of a body and then be unable to do anything at all with the result.
strengths: sees in the dark in a cavern system where nothing else alive can, and has done it since childhood
reads what a body is carrying more accurately than anyone trained to, because she has had to reverse-engineer the instrument
knows the mortuary method well enough to state its precise limits in front of the office that applies it
does not require herself to be reassured, which makes her unusually safe to be in a room with
keeps a record of her own kind's readings in her head and has never once mislaid it
weaknesses: nothing in her body is repaired, so every cost she has ever paid is still being paid
her span is a fraction of her parent's and she has no way to spend it on anything that outlasts her
she cannot leave the caves, and nothing in the setting has ever needed her outside them
her accuracy is filed under another body, so the one thing she is good at produces no standing whatever
she has stopped pressing, and stopping is indistinguishable from accepting
reference_stats.combat_read: Anywhere there is no light she is the only one present who can see, which is worth a great deal in a cavern and worth nothing on any ground with a horizon. She has no practice, no frame for it and no reason to have one. In a fight she is a person who can find the exit and cannot leave it.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is institutional rather than invented. Her kind's advantage is that they see and their parents cannot, which is authored in the subspecies record and is the reason the subspecies is named for it. The cost is the same record: the bloom renews nothing, so nothing in her body is being repaired, and they live a fraction of their parent's span. Both halves are in the species record and neither is mine. What is mine is the reading that connects the two: the discipline that makes her valuable is the discipline that produced the instrument that cannot tell her from her parent's cousin. Nothing mechanical has been added here. No technique, no item and no change of frame gives the register a second reading method, and the register's refusal of the village-memory alternative is its founding argument rather than an oversight. Her species carries no ceiling and closes no path, and that is a fact about the absence of a limit and not a claim that she has nothing to climb; she is on no ladder and the record does not put her on one.

canon.role_in_story: The mortal tier spends all three of its law slots on physical, life and qi. That is not a fact about the world; it is the reason the world here has a plough, a roof and a levy and cannot also afford a profession. The Three-Law Primer is the tier's entire curriculum and it is taught as a closed list rather than as a foundation, because a three-slot frame cannot carry a fourth subject and because a pupil who wants to know what his world is missing has to go up the stair, which he cannot afford. She is the body this curriculum was written for. She is the ordinary one, the one the world has no opinion about, and her species closes the mind path outright because a frame this even has no native faculty for it. That absence is the quietest fact about her and it is also the whole of her advantage: nothing in her is quietly failing for want of a subject she cannot take, so a teacher can put three subjects in front of her without the fourth subject's hole showing through as a defect. She is the one pupil the closed list fits exactly. She is also the reason the closed list can never be opened, because the only subject a commonborn lacks is the one that tier is not written for, and every institution on this ground has concluded independently that it can therefore teach her, and none of them has concluded she is worth a certificate. A household on the plains does not hold a plot and does not hold an office. It holds a numbered place in a queue for tenure, because the queue cannot be shortened by anybody and a family with no slot has no claim at all. Tenure is not an office. A queue is not a seat. Every seat in this setting is filled by certifying something, and the thing Ordrie has instead of a certification is a number inked on her wrist and renewed twice a season since she was nine. So she is unaffiliated, and the reason is institutional and arithmetic and has nothing to do with her body refusing anything: the ground issues claims in plots, her household holds a place in a line of plots, and the one subject she could be distinguished for is the subject the ground was never built to want. She is not on a ladder and she has never gone looking, and the absence is not modesty. She has looked.
canon.first_appearance: Asked, at the end of a Primer sitting, what she intended to do afterwards, and gave the answer the household had already given her: wait for the queue. The teacher, who had taught the closed list to three generations of the same kind of child and had never once been asked a question by one of them, asked her instead what she was good at, and she thought about it long enough that the room began to make other noise.
canon.lore:
A commonborn is the body everybody is born into before the world has an opinion about them. The species record puts the consequence in one flat sentence: nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so a commonborn has to settle on one early, and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest. That sentence is usually read as a description of mediocrity and it is better read as a description of a slot. On a tier that licenses exactly three laws, the specialists are not rare and noble; they are the bodies the tier was built around. A stoneborn is what the tier uses when the ground has to carry. A marshfolk is what it uses when the ground has to be wet. Those two occupy the two subjects the tier can afford to name, and the ordinary body is left with the residue, which is not a smaller version of the work but the part of the work nobody organises.

The Primer is the whole curriculum and it is a closed list. Physical, life, qi, taught in that order, taught as a list rather than as a foundation, and the reason is stated and is not a philosophy: a three-slot frame cannot carry a fourth subject. A pupil who wants to know what his world is missing has to go up the stair to find out, and cannot afford the stair. That is the entire educational position of the lowest tier in this setting, and it is honest, and it is the single most consequential thing about the ground.

Here is what nobody has counted, because there is nothing to count. Her species closes the mind path outright. The record's reason is that a body this even has no native faculty for introspection at all, and that is an absence rather than a bar. So the fourth subject is not something she could have taken if the frame were wider; it is something she was never issued. Which means the Primer's closed list, in her case, is not three of four. It is all three, and it fits. She is the one body on the tier for whom the closed curriculum is exactly the right size, and this is the only advantage she has ever been able to put in a sentence.

The cost of it is that the same absence is why nothing on this ground wants to certify her. A certificate in this setting is a claim that a body has done a thing reliably enough to be relied on. A commonborn's body is reliable at nothing in particular and faultless at everything ordinary, and there is no office whose business is ordinary excellence, because ordinary excellence is what the household assumes when it hands someone a barrow. The tier cannot afford a professional. That is the plain-dweller commons in one sentence: the plough, the roof and the levy are three claims on the same hands, so tenure is not an office, it is a queue. Her family holds no plot and no office. It holds a numbered place in a queue for tenure, and the number is renewed twice a season, and there is no arrangement by which anybody moves a household further up that line, because moving the queue would be shortening it.

So she has two absences and they are not the same shape. One is anatomical and total: no faculty for the fourth subject, which closes nothing she could have opened and costs her nothing she can name. The other is institutional and total: the ground issues claims in plots, and her household's claim is a position in a line of plots, and the line is not an office, and nobody is seated on a line. Every seat in this setting is filled by certifying something, and what she has instead is a number on the inside of her wrist. That is the entire reason she is unaffiliated. She is not a body that failed a test. She is a body the testing never had a use for, holding a claim that cannot be spent on anything.

The reading she resists is the flattering one. She is not a hidden specialist who has not yet recognised herself, and she has tested that reading carefully enough to discard it, because nothing about her own frame answers any of the questions a hidden specialist's frame answers. She is not a body that refused a door. Nobody in her household has ever held a door open and told her to walk through it, and she has not gone looking for one, and the reason is not modesty and not discouragement. It is that the subjects she could be taught are the subjects the ground already has a specialist for, and she would be the second body asked to do a job that this tier's single law slots were designed to be spent on somebody better at it than her.

What she does instead is the work that has no name and no holder. She reads a Primer three times, teaches the closed list to children younger than she was when she learned it, and knows which of the three subjects each of them will fail and why, because the failure is always the same one and it is always the frame rather than the child. This makes her, in the only sense the word can hold on this ground, the best teacher of the closed list in the district, and it is worth exactly nothing, because a teacher is certified and she cannot be, and because the only thing a certificate buys on the plains is a shorter wait in a queue that cannot be shortened.
history: Inked with her household's queue number at nine, the first time the number was renewed onto a child rather than copied forward.
Learned the closed list at the usual age and was the only one in her year who asked no question, which her teacher noted and did not know what to make of.
Began teaching the Primer to younger children because the arrangement needed an adult in the room and she was the one available.
Worked out, from her own frame and not from anyone telling her, that the fourth subject was not withheld from her and was never going to be issued.
Was asked once by a visitor from a wider tier what she intended to do afterwards, and gave the household's answer, and then could not stop thinking about the question for a season.

personality.summary: The ordinary body on the lowest tier, whose species has no faculty for the one subject the ground was never written to name, which makes her the closed curriculum's exact fit and its least certificated pupil at the same time. She has the queue number and the district's best grasp of the closed list and no institution on the plains wants either, and she has stopped finding that surprising.

relationships.note: The body everybody is born into before the world has an opinion about them. Nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so a commonborn settles on one early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest, and the mind path is closed outright because a frame this even has no native faculty for introspection at all. That absence is an absence rather than a bar, which is the whole of her in one distinction.

The mortal tier's whole curriculum, taught as a closed list rather than as a foundation because a three-slot frame cannot carry a fourth subject. She is the one body on the tier for whom that closed list is exactly the right size, because the only subject she lacks is the one this tier was never written to name.

A plains clan that holds no plot and no office, only a numbered place in a queue for tenure, because on ground where distance is not conserved the plough, the roof and the levy are three claims on the same hands. A family with no queue slot has no claim at all and the queue cannot be shortened by anybody, so the number on her wrist is the whole of what she can lay claim to.

The commons of the plains: a hundred-year body, a ceiling of eight realms and a frame seating only three laws, so nobody here expects to ascend and the work is judged by what survives the season. The culture cannot afford a professional, which is why the best teacher of the closed list in her district has nothing to be paid for and no certificate to teach under.

First gate on the path her species has no faculty for, and the only one of the ladder's entry points whose cost is written as leaving a body. She can read what it asks for and has no native capacity that the asking would improve, which is why the closed list does not feel like a limit to her and cannot be widened by anybody who tries.

The only ground on the plains where the tier's one herb grows, and therefore the tier's only medicine, dye and calories at once. It cannot be fenced around a slow crop, which is the reason her household holds a place in a line rather than a plot, and the reason the line is the only form of claim the ground issues.

She is the most reliable unremarkable person in a district that has no use for reliable unremarkableness.

She is the most patient person in any room and the least dangerous, and the honest assessment is that a settlement with a teacher like her is a settlement that will not lose a generation to a mistake and will not win a fight either.

Anatomically, her species closes the mind path outright because a frame this even has no native faculty for introspection, so the fourth subject is an absence rather than a bar and the closed list fits her exactly. Institutionally, the tier issues claims in plots and her household holds a position in a line of plots, because the culture cannot afford a professional and tenure is a queue rather than an office. The two halves do not touch, and that is the point: the absence that makes her the curriculum's exact fit is the same absence that makes her unworth certificating, and both facts come from two different records in the bible. canon.role_in_story: His species was made by crossing the fire body with the ash body and the cross buys a rate nothing else in this setting reaches. It is also the shortest-lived cultivator any record here describes: the fire half keeps the ash sieve hot enough to process faster and scar faster, and the reputation for being the best and the briefest of his kind is a single fact rather than two. What is unusual about Orrin is not the rate. It is that the discipline built for his kind is built for one session. The Quench Order is a discipline of bankers rather than a school of thought: it teaches the deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows, because the fastest bodies in this setting have no elemental law seated beneath them to spend into, so every overflow has to be absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired. It closes permanently the moment the body is lit. Every emberhollow is lit before he is born. So Orrin is the one member of his kind for whom the teaching arrives and is immediately, permanently unavailable, and he has been a member of an order that finished with him before he could sit in it. That is his unaffiliation, and it is institutional before it is anything else: nobody refused him. The Order took him in on the strength of exactly the property that ends it, and then could not proceed. He is the standing exception to the only profession his body actually qualifies for. He has never been on a ladder and there is nothing to climb toward, because his species stops at the eighth gate for a reason his ash parent's record states and he inherits without alteration. What he does instead is the work that survives his own schedule: he stands at the ley's edge and prices other people's fire, and he does it in the one currency the belt has, which is time, and his time is the fastest-burning thing on the fan.
canon.first_appearance: Was already standing at the ley's edge when the party came up the ash road, not because he had been waiting but because there was nowhere else on that ground a person of his kind could stand for any length of time. He offered to tell them what their fire was worth and what it was costing them, in that order and in the same breath, and did not say a second word about himself for the length of the consultation. When the woman from the company asked how long he could keep this up, he gave her a number, and then gave her a smaller one, and told her plainly which of the two he believed.
canon.lore:
An emberhollow is a fire body crossed with an ash body and the two halves do not have a good relationship. The fire half keeps the sieve hot enough that it processes faster; processing faster is the whole of the cross's advantage and also the whole of its cost, because faster processing in that frame means faster scarring. His species holds the eighth gate for exactly the reason his ash parent cannot pass it, and worse, and the record is plain that the faster it burns out trying the better it has done. Its reputation for being the best and the shortest-lived cultivator in any record is one fact rather than two, and anybody who quotes either half alone is quoting something the bible refuses.

What is peculiar about his situation is not anatomical. It is that the one profession his body qualifies for is closed by the qualification.

The Quench Order is a discipline of bankers rather than a school of thought. It teaches the deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows. Its reason for existing is written into its own record: the fastest bodies in this setting have no elemental law seated beneath them to spend into, so every overflow has to be absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired. That is his condition exactly, and it is the condition the discipline was invented to serve. The fastest body on the belt has no seat beneath it to vent into. It has to be taught to spend itself on purpose, in small amounts, at chosen moments, instead of all at once and by accident.

And the Order closes permanently the moment the body is lit.

Every emberhollow is lit before he is born. The fire half of the cross is not a thing that is acquired at a gate; it is the thing the body is made of. So the Order takes him in. It takes in every member of his kind, because the property that makes him the fastest body here is the property that makes him the discipline's intended subject, and the Order would be failing at its purpose if it turned him away. And then it cannot proceed, because proceeding requires a furnace that is not yet lit, and his furnace was lit at his conception, and the Order's closing condition is not a rule it enforces afterwards. It is the definition of what it is.

He is therefore the only permanent member of the only discipline his species qualifies for. Not the only member. The only one who cannot leave, and the leaving is the closing. There is no version of the teaching that reaches him, because the teaching is aimed at the interval before ignition and he has no interval.

He has done the arithmetic that this forces and he has done it honestly. His species holds the eighth gate. The reason is authored: the eighth gate completes the ordinary meridian set at the liver, the ash parent's mineral load filters through that organ, and it is the first organ to fail under the burden. The fire parent adds a heavier mineral load to a blood already filtering stone, so the organ that fails fails sooner. His parent could not hold the last ordinary meridian. He cannot hold it, and he burns out trying. So the thing he would be climbing toward, if he climbed, is eight gates and a wall, and the wall is not closed to him by the discipline that failed him. It is closed by his parent's organ. Those are two different reasons and both of them are true and neither of them is the Quench Order.

He is precise about this distinction and it is the thing that separates him from his own kind's folklore. There is a version of his life in the belt where he is a man thwarted by a rule, and he refuses it. The rule did not do this. The rule stopped being relevant before it reached him. What did this is his frame, and the frame would have done it whether or not the discipline existed. He has told people this more than once and has been told, politely, that it does not comfort anybody, and he agrees that it does not and says so.

The work he does instead is pricing fire, and it is worth recording what that is. He stands at the ley's edge and tells the people who come to the ley what their fire is worth and what it is costing them. The two are not the same number and everybody who comes up the ash road wants them to be. He is the best read on that fan because the fastest body on a fan reads heat the way a specialist reads their own medium, and the number he gives is exact, and it is exact about his own position in the trade without any effort on his part, which is the part he finds harder than the arithmetic.

He has no roster anywhere on the fan. Not because anyone has refused him; the belt's institutions do not keep rolls of people the way the plains does. He has no roster because there is no office to be rolled into. The one rite that would put a question about his own body into a durable place requires the answer to be entered in a register by a named party, and the belt does not do that, and he has decided that what he does not get entered is the only part of his situation he can still be honest about. That is not grievance. It is the reason he has not spent himself on making a record where one does not exist. The record would be about his fire. He has enough of that.

What he wants, stated as plainly as his species permits, is a season. Not more than he can spend and not measured against anybody. A season of work he does not have to finish quickly, on ground where the work exists, doing the thing he is actually good at, at a rate somebody else chooses. He has never had one and has no arrangement by which he could expect one, and he has stopped describing the want as anything larger than it is, which took most of a decade and is the single hardest thing in this record to convey to somebody reading about him.
history: Taken into the Quench Order at the standard intake, on the strength of the one property that made him the best subject the discipline had ever been offered, and stood as its only permanent member from that afternoon.
Worked out, unaided and before anyone said it to him, that the discipline's closing condition was his own birth and that no part of it would ever reach him.
Took the first pricing work at the ley's edge at sixteen, because the fan does not keep a roll of anybody and a boy who can read heat has nothing to enrol in.
Corrected a visiting factor, in front of a company, on the difference between what a fire is worth and what it costs to keep lit.
Began giving two numbers where the belt's trade expects one, and has never yet been asked to explain the smaller one.

canon.role_in_story: Every appointment in this setting passes a trial the naming office cannot judge. That rule was written after an attempt that came very nearly to filling four vacant immortal seats by decree, and its entire defence against a polity that promotes itself is a single sentence: the highest office here may name a seat and may not take one. The reason the rule holds is that nobody who can be judged can be seated. Hesper cannot. A thornhost is the one configuration in which a thornline colony and a commonborn host both reach old age, and the colony stops at the eighth gate and the host inherits that stop, so the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's and the whole legal problem is stated as a number. She is also, in the sect that swears her, the one person who holds two offices in one body and cannot vacate either without dying. Every sworn member who holds no office sits at the open door, and recognition begins where office begins, and she cannot be brought to the door because holding the door would require holding an office and she already holds two she cannot empty. So the one seat in this setting that requires no office is the one seat she cannot be given. That is not a refusal and she has never made one. It is the collision of two authored arrangements that both work: a rule that says no unjudgeable body may be seated, and a body whose seating would end two terms nobody can end. She is unaffiliated because the ladder's entry points are appointments, and appointments are trials, and she is the one person in this setting who cannot be tried.
canon.first_appearance: Was standing at a gate on the flats where the ground cannot be measured, waiting to open it for whoever came, and had been there long enough that a passing household assumed she was the keeper. She corrected them, at some length, and then did not correct the second household, and then asked the second household's child a question that made the child stop and think, and the reason she stopped correcting them is the reason she is where she is.
canon.lore:
A thornhost is a pairing that completed rather than failed. A thornline's spore has to be implanted in a living body to finish developing, so the free form exists only as a spore and the adult form exists only as half of somebody else. The colony wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and cannot cross the host's liver, which is the first organ large and dense enough to resist it, and the colony has been observed on the far side of that organ and it stops there. That is the eighth gate and it is the colony's ceiling rather than the host's. The host could have gone on. The hybrid cannot. This species is the case the thornline record means when it says a body's liability is inherited rather than authored, and it is the only case in the record where a liability is inherited rather than chosen.

Her frame is a commonborn frame. The host supplies the frame, the throughput and the only reachable registry, and neither half is anatomically dominant, so the boundary between them is visible only under instrumentation and she has never once been asked to submit to any. She has a second channel that carries the colony's read on her own qi, and she has never been able to close it and has stopped trying. Above the two of them, the whole thing presents as one throat node she cannot reach, one mean line running along the inner arm, and a diet that is ordinary food plus whatever the colony draws: small, steady, and cheaper than an uncolonised body of the same size.

Now the institutions, which is where her situation actually is.

Every appointment in this setting passes a trial the naming office cannot judge. The rule exists because the highest office here may name a seat and may not take one, and that single sentence is the whole defence against a polity that promotes itself. Its method is uncontroversial: if you cannot be judged you cannot be seated. It was written by an attempt that came very nearly to filling four vacant immortal seats by decree, and the whole point of it is that the four vacant seats stay vacant rather than being filled by anybody who could not be judged into them.

And the sect that swears her has a seat for people who hold no office. Everyone sworn who holds no office sits at the open door in all but name, and it recognises nothing at all, because recognition begins where office begins. That is the one place in this setting where a person can be present without holding anything, and it is the seat Hesper cannot take.

She holds two offices in one body. That is the dispute the sect and the house are actually fighting about, and she is the whole of it stated as a person rather than as a question: whether office is inside the house or outside it, and it cannot be split because the sect's recognition begins where office begins and the house's protection ends in exactly the same place. Her own situation is the mirror of the sentence. She holds offices on both sides of it. She cannot vacate either, because vacating means separating two entangled souls on one meridian set and separation is known to be lethal to both, so the vacancy would not be a vacancy. It would be a death, twice, and an appointment that no calendar survives.

So the door is closed to her for a reason that is structural and not personal. She cannot be brought to it because she is already holding the two things she would have to give up. She cannot be seated on the ladder for the same reason, by the same mechanism, because a ladder seat is an appointment and an appointment is a trial and she cannot be judged, cannot be replaced and cannot be separated into two candidates.

What is striking about this is that no institution did anything to her. The sect is not expelling her; the door is for everyone who holds no office and she happens to hold two. The naming office is not excluding her; the trial is for everyone and she is the one body the trial cannot be run on. Every rule is working. The rules were each written by somebody who had been hurt by the failure of the rule before it, and she is what the rules do when they succeed.

She has made her position legible to herself with unusual clarity and she holds it without heat. The arch she cannot cross is the arch of the gate she keeps. There is an arrangement for a marked threshold: a household marks its own door, renews the mark when the frame beneath it changes, and admits that a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not, because an unwritten law is not a weak law but an absent one, with no dial and nothing to push, so a community that needs a guarantee of welcome has to build one at the door. She keeps the best-kept mark on the flats. The mark carries the obligation. The obligation survives the household that cut it. A traveller is admitted because the door says so and not because she agreed. That is the protection she actually has, and she is clear-eyed about its price: it protects her almost perfectly and it does so by making her unnecessary as a party to it. Nobody has ever been refused at her gate. She has never once refused anybody anything. Both of those facts are the same fact.

What she has instead of the door is a body that is legible. The colony's growth is visible on her in the way jade cleft moss is legible on the rock that holds its qi and dies back over any cut ground, and the settlement has been reading the mean line on her arm for longer than she has been standing at this gate. Nobody maintains it. It is only what has happened to her body. She is the longest continuous record of her own household's reserves in the district and she has never declared it and never been asked, and that is a thing to be careful about in any telling of her: the settlement uses her arm as a calendar without having decided to, and she has never corrected them, and the reason she has not is the same reason she does not take the door.

Because to be seated is to be liable, and she is already liable for two things that cannot be ended. She has run this out and she does not think it can be run the other way: a person who could be emptied of her offices could be seated, and a person who could be seated would have to be emptied, and she cannot be emptied without dying twice. She is not on a ladder. Her species stops at the eighth gate for a reason her parent's organ gives, and the mind path is closed to her in the colony's own right, so the paths are not the difficulty and she is careful never to describe them as the difficulty. The difficulty is that the setting's method of admitting anybody to anything is a trial, and she is the one body in the setting the trial cannot be run on.
history: Implanted as a spore in a commonborn host's body and integrated rather than fatal, which happens rarely and by nobody's intention, and is the only configuration in which both halves reach old age.
Inherited the colony's stop at the eighth gate, so a frame that could have continued inherited a ceiling it did not choose and cannot give up without dying.
Sworn into a house and a sect and given office in both, and discovered that the house's protection ends exactly where the sect's recognition begins.
Found the sect's open door and worked out that the only seat requiring no office is the one she cannot be given, because she holds two she cannot vacate.
Began keeping the best-kept threshold mark on the flats and has never once refused a traveller, and has never once been asked whether she wanted the obligation.

relationships.note: The one configuration in which a thornline colony and a host both reach old age. The colony stops at the eighth gate and the host inherits that stop, so the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's, which is the whole legal problem stated as a number: a person who cannot ascend for a reason they did not choose and cannot give up without dying.

The first organ large and dense enough to resist a tendril layer, and the reason the colony's routing stops where it stops. The host's own capacity is irrelevant past that point. She has never asked the question of what would happen if the two of them could be separated, because the answer is authored and it is lethal to both.

Every appointment in both polities passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and the rule exists because the highest office may name a seat and may not take one. Its method is that if you cannot be judged you cannot be seated, and she cannot be judged, cannot be replaced and cannot be separated into two candidates, so the rule that protects the setting from a bad appointment is also what permanently excludes this one.

Every sworn member of the house who holds no office is a Ward and every sworn member of the sect who holds no office sits at the open door. She is the one person in the setting who holds two offices in one body and cannot vacate either without dying, which is the dispute's whole problem stated as a person rather than as a question.

The Church of Names empties the chair and keeps the entry open so the calendar continues uninterrupted, because an office outlives its holder by construction. Her case is the living instance and the limit of it: two occupants, one chair, and no possibility of either vacating without ending the term, so the rite that handles a vacancy cannot be run on her at all.

The mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because certifying a death needs a body and separating two entangled souls is known to be lethal to both. She is the population that produces cases by existing, and she is alive, which makes her the one instance of the problem that has not yet needed the seal.

reference_stats.summary: She is not a combatant and would be a poor one. What she is for is standing in a doorway and being the most reliable welcome on a road, which is a real and unglamorous competence that she has never had to try at. She also cannot be appointed, cannot be judged, and cannot be relieved, and all three of those are the same fact about her body rather than three separate disabilities.
strengths: admits reliably: the mark she keeps is the most dependable welcome in the district and it has never once failed
cheaper to keep than any body of her size, which is the strongest single piece of evidence that the arrangement is not disease

reference_stats.combat_read: She would be removed from any live exchange early and correctly, because there is no posture available to her that turns a body with an integrated tendril layer into anything else. Read from the other side, she is the hardest person on a road to displace: nobody can relieve her, nobody can replace her, and the thing that keeps the road open is a mark she renews herself.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is anatomical and institutional, and both halves are authored rather than invented. Anatomically, the colony cannot cross the host's liver, so the hybrid's ceiling is the colony's and the host could have gone on and the hybrid cannot, which is the species record's own sentence. Institutionally, every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and the rule's method is that an unjudgeable body cannot be seated, while the one seat that requires no office cannot be given to somebody who holds two that cannot be vacated. What is mine is only the joining observation that the two arrangements are individually sound and jointly produce her exclusion, and that no rule in either was written with her in mind. Nothing mechanical has been added. No technique, item or change of frame gives the tendril layer a passage through the liver, no office in the setting waives a trial on the ground that the trial is inconvenient, and no rite empties two occupants out of one chair without ending the term.

canon.role_in_story: Every institution in this setting keeps a list of what a body is, and the mortuary college at the bottom of the list is the Field Registry, which reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, on the ground that a village that may amend its dead may amend its standing. The register's method is a reading. It takes a frame and reports which groups that frame has seated. It is the most useful thing in the setting and the reason nobody publishes it, and it works everywhere a frame is a frame. A marshfolk is a wading amphibian lineage: three points of contact over a splayed flat foot and a tail-prop, and the heel never takes a full load, so qi never pools there and the two heel vessels that the fourteenth gate wants simultaneously are not a thing her anatomy has anywhere. She walks fine. She cannot stand still, and the distinction is the whole of her. And here is the problem with the register: a frame is read by naming what it has, and this body has no organ the reading can point at. Three points of contact and a prop are not organs. The reading comes back with a number where her anatomy has a shape, and the number is not wrong, it is a reading of the wrong kind of thing, and the register has no line for that distinction because the register does not know the distinction exists. So the most exact recorder of what a body is in this setting cannot record her, and she is the one population on the floodplain whose body settles every question about it and cannot be entered. That is her unaffiliation. It is institutional, it is not a refusal, and it is not a ceiling either: she can be taught, and nobody has taught her, because there is nowhere to put her.
canon.first_appearance: Was reading a channel bottom by pressure with both palms flat and the water to her knee, and a field crew from the registry came down the bank to ask her to stand still so they could read her. She said she could. They waited. She shifted onto the tail-prop and then onto the front foot and then back again, and explained, patiently and three times, that there was no version of standing still on three points. They wrote something down. She asked to see it and read it upside down at their own hand, and did not say anything else about it.
canon.lore:
A marshfolk is neither a tidecaller nor a commonborn but the body in between, and the record is blunt about why: the three-point stance that lets her move through silt never loads a heel, and qi never pools where a heel would be. That is what her kind's ordinary gates are cleared on, and the fourteenth is the first gate that wants both heel vessels at once. They exist to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other half, which is the only ground on this tier that answers to neither season.

She is the best body on the margin for the work that has to be done in water that will not hold a foot. Reading a channel bed by pressure through the sole rather than by eye, feeling where the shelf drops before a loaded barrow goes over it, walking silt that a two-pointed body would come to rest in. She has done it since she could hold a barrow handle, and she does it with the tail-prop as a rudder in a way nobody has found a better answer to. The commons does not praise. It sends the barrow to whoever is standing in the right water. That is the whole of her standing and it is not nothing.

Now the register, which is where her case actually is.

The Field Registry is the college that keeps the burnt list. Its method is stated without apology: at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and it exists because a life that stopped at a limit nobody was issued is a record too. Behind the method is the Composition Survey, which is the most useful thing in this setting and the reason nobody publishes it: count the groups a frame has actually seated, not the groups its tier is permitted to apply, because the difference between the two is what a mortal world spends its whole life inside without ever knowing. That is a reading. It takes a frame and asks what is in it.

A marshfolk frame has three points of contact, a splayed flat foot and a prehensile tail-prop. None of those is an organ. There is no heart analogue to name, no paired structure to run a channel between, nothing the instrument can point at and say what it has found. The reading does not fail on her; it succeeds, and returns a number, and the number is a correct count of a class of thing that her anatomy does not instantiate. That is the failure, and it is the kind nothing catches, because a wrong reading looks exactly like a right one and the register exists precisely so that nobody has to adjudicate between a frame's reading and a village's memory.

And the register is where she has to appear. The college keeps a sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because certifying a death needs a body and the frames keep producing the record without it. A settlement on the margin produces her kind routinely and reads none of them. So she is the one population on the floodplain whose body settles every question asked about it and cannot be entered in the book that answers them. She is not on a ladder. She has never been offered a seat, and the reason is that there is no institution on this ground that has a line for a body shaped the way she is.

This is not the same as a ceiling. Her kind clears the gate set and stops where the heel would be. The fourteenth gate wants both heel vessels simultaneously and she has no heel and no structure in its place, so that gate is a wall rather than a step, and she is entirely clear that a wall at fourteen is not the reason she is where she is, because the reason she is where she is would be identical on a body with feet. She is careful about this and she corrects people who get it wrong, and she has corrected a great many people, and the correction has never once changed her situation.

What the settlement has instead is her body read informally by people who are not the college and are not wrong. She moves three points in an hour and the people who have watched her long enough can tell her mood from which point she is standing on, which is not an instrument and is not a record and could not survive being written down by anyone who had not spent a winter watching. Her children are the easiest thing in the district to recognise and the hardest to enter.

The pressure that keeps her where she is is not subtle and it is not the register's fault. Any appointment in this setting passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and the trial is the method of seating anybody anywhere. So the question of what a marshfolk body is was settled at the founding of the college by an instrument that does not have an answer for her, and everything downstream of that founding has inherited the settlement. She has read the college's method. She can state its limits better than any clerk she has spoken to. She has written twice. Both letters were filed, and the college charges for the file, which is its standing revenue and not its failure.

So she does the other thing, and the other thing is what the flood does. She reads the channel. She reads it by pressure through the sole, which is an instrument nobody had to build and nobody has thought to write down, and which is the only reading of a marshfolk frame that this setting has ever produced that is actually about her. She has been the barrow-woman on the margin for longer than she cares to count. What she is waiting for is not a gate. There is nothing on the ladder she is refusing and nothing on it she has been invited to. She is waiting for somebody to read a bed the way she reads one, which is a lower bar than it sounds and has not been cleared in her lifetime.
history: Hatched from a woven reed mat and carried under the brood pouch through a dry season, which for her kind is the ordinary way into the world and not an event.
Walked her first barrow at nine, on the front foot, because she was the only one small enough to be put between the handle and the bank.
Stood for a registry reading on the margin at fourteen and discovered that a body with three points of contact and a tail-prop has no entry in the instrument that keeps the list.
Learned to read a bed by pressure through the sole after being told twice by a field crew that she could not stand still to be read.
Wrote to the Field Registry setting out the limits of the composition reading, and the letter was filed, and the college charges for the file.

relationships.note: A wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, so it is neither a tidecaller nor a commonborn but the body in between. Three points of contact over a splayed flat foot and a tail-prop, and the heel never takes a full load, so qi never pools there and the fourteenth gate, which wants both heel vessels at once, is a wall rather than a step.

Tier 5, the first meridian added after the entry gate, and the one place both readings of the ladder agree on. She has one, and it is not the organ a composition survey points at, because a survey names organs and her frame's load paths are three contacts and a prop, which is not a thing any instrument in this setting was built to name.

Its authored work is bookkeeping rather than strength: it holds what the body has decided not to spend, and damage here exhausts quietly and last, which is why it goes unreported for years. On a frame that never loads a heel and never pools qi in one place, that is the only description of how a charge gets held, and it is not an organ she can point at either.

The college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify because certifying a death needs a body. Her settlement produces her kind routinely and reads none of it, because the reading names organs and she has three points of contact and a prop, so the instrument succeeds and returns a number for a class of thing her body does not instantiate.

Count the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups its tier permits, because the difference between the two is what a mortal world spends its whole life inside without knowing. It is the most useful thing in the setting and the reason nobody publishes it, and it has no answer for a body whose load paths are not organs.

The band beside the run where flood water stands after the channel has emptied, and the only ground on the plains with standing shallow water through the dry season. What she can put into it is a function of her own mass and her own reach, so the ground's usefulness to her is a number that falls whenever she gets better at the only thing she is good at.

reference_stats.summary: She fights the way the ground lets her: from inside it, in contact with it, weight low and moving, closing with all three points rather than driving from one. She does not fight well and she does not fight often. What she is for is holding a position in a channel while somebody else does the thing that matters, and she has held one against current longer than most people in this setting have been standing.
strengths: reads a bed, a bank and a current by pressure through the sole alone, in the dark and under load
cannot be moved while she is braced on three points, which is a different kind of immovability from a stance
moves through silt that will not hold a two-pointed foot and carries a load while doing it
carries far more than a wader of her apparent weight is expected to carry
the tail-prop is a rudder and nobody has found a better answer to that
weaknesses: cannot stand still, so every hold she attempts needs the one posture her frame will not give
there is a depth beyond which she is simply a heavy object in moving water
her skin dries fast out of the water and the dry season is a long stretch of careful scheduling
her advantage and her usefulness are measured by the same falling number
the instrument that records what a body is has never read her, so nothing she does can be entered anywhere
reference_stats.combat_read: Anywhere soft, shallow and slow, she is close to unkillable and there is no counter the ground provides. On anything hard, she is out of her depth before the exchange starts, and the honest reading is that she has no fighting ground outside the one place she is standing in. She would be told to hold a line and she would hold it, and the line would be a channel.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with a cost that is anatomical rather than invented, and the pair is the same fact seen twice. Her species never loads a heel, so the stance that would make her immovable is the one stance she cannot hold. Three points of contact and a tail-prop carry her through silt no other body crosses, and they are also a frame with no organ for the composition survey to name, which is why the setting's own recorder cannot enter her. Both halves are as the species and the survey records state them. What is mine is only the observation that a body shaped by load paths rather than organs defeats an instrument that counts organs, and that this is a successful reading of the wrong kind of thing rather than a failed one. Nothing mechanical is asserted anywhere in this block. No technique, item or change of frame gives her a heel or a structure in its place, the fourteenth gate stays a wall at fourteen rather than a step, and the registry's method stays a reading rather than a ruling.
